newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL OVERNIGHT RATE FALLS AFTER BILL MATURITY.
newsitem.headline: KL OVERNIGHT RATE FALLS AFTER BILL MATURITY.

text.p: The overnight interbank rate fell to 5.8/9 percent on Friday after the maturity of a one-billion ringgit Bank Negara bill issue, dealers said.
The overnight traded from a high of 6.5 percent, against its close of 6.2/3 percent on Thursday.
Dealers said apart from continued offers from foreign banks, there was also fresh lending by local banks.
"The lenders were mostly principal dealers who now have some fresh funds following the maturity," said a dealer at a Malaysian bank.
In the morning, other interbank rates were also softer because of the bill maturity which has helped ease market tightness.
Friday's maturity of Bank Negara bills has not been rolled over.
One-week interbank rate was down at 7.0 percent against 7.5 percent on Thursday.
One-month money was at 7.8/9 percent against 7.8/8.0 percent, while three-month was at 7.85/95 percent against 7.9/8.0 percent.
"The market is still quite tight and rates are unlikely to fall much from current levels unless there is a big inflow," said another dealer.
